title: About
text: The lectures are by Yiqing Xu, Department of Political Science, Stanford University. Version 1.0.0 was released in September 2026.

title: About
text:
Credits
Much of the material builds on joint work and on colleagues’ slides.

Lecture 3 follows Xu, Zhao, and Ding (2026), with the application from Cao, Xu, and Zhang (2022, Journal of Development Economics) and the fdid R package.
Lectures 4 and 5 draw on the reanalysis study with Albert Chiu, Xingchen Lan, and Ziyi Liu (Chiu, Lan, Liu, and Xu 2026). The replication figures in Lecture 5 come from that project.
Lectures 1 and 2 build on teaching slides by Jens Hainmueller, as noted on their reference slides.
Lecture 6 uses Luke Sanford’s Benin land-titling example and, on the synthetic difference-in-differences slides, figures from the authors’ slides (Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens, and Wager). Both are credited on the slides.

title: Teaching with the slides
text:
Building and adapting the slides
The repository has the LaTeX Beamer source of every deck, every figure, and the R scripts that redraw the figures from data or by simulation. All references sit in one file, references.bib, so each deck’s reference list is rebuilt from it. With TeX Live 2023 or later, make builds the six handouts and make animated the versions with animations. The README has the details, and SOURCES.md records where every figure comes from.
All six decks share one look, set in common/. To change the colors of every deck, edit the four colors at the top of common/theme.tex.

title: Lectures on Causal Panel Analysis
text:
Slides for six lectures of 100 to 120 minutes each on causal inference with panel data. The lectures are for applied researchers and graduate students in the social sciences who work with panel data. Each method is introduced through an example and a picture, and formulas appear only where the ideas need them.
The page counts link to the PDFs, which have one page per slide. To present with the step-by-step reveals, build that version from the LaTeX source (make animated). “Code” opens the lecture’s folder on GitHub: the LaTeX source, the figures, and the R scripts that draw them.

title: Lectures on Causal Panel Analysis
text:
The arc
Lectures 1 and 2 cover the parametric panel toolkit and the canonical difference-in-differences design. Lecture 3 extends that design to events that affect everyone (factorial difference-in-differences). Lecture 4 diagnoses three problems with two-way fixed effects: the design problem (what strict exogeneity implies for treatment assignment), violations of parallel trends, and the weighting problem when effects differ across units. Lecture 5 repairs the weighting problem with estimators that allow effects to differ, and works through three applications from a large reanalysis study. Lecture 6 turns to synthetic control, factor models, and doubly and triply robust estimators, which handle some violations of parallel trends.

The field is moving fast, and these slides lean toward the author’s own research and understanding of it. Read them as one path through the material rather than as a survey.

title: Lectures on Causal Panel Analysis
text:
Software
The R packages used in the lectures, with tutorials:

fect: fixed effects counterfactual estimators.
gsynth: the generalized synthetic control method.
fdid: factorial difference-in-differences.
panelView: visualizing panel data.
